objects.title: Evidence-First AI Decisions
objects.summary: AI-derived business state should keep exact source evidence, validate model output with a schema, and keep model confidence separate from deterministic business scoring.
boundaries: Proposed from one reference project; not independently validated as universal.
Does not prove model quality or production runtime behavior.

objects.title: Durable Async Side Effects
objects.summary: Slow or external work should be committed/enqueued before execution, claimed idempotently, and monitored with stale lease recovery that is actually invoked.
boundaries: The positive pattern is repo-observed; the audit also proved a production blocker when recovery is not wired into the live loop.

objects.title: Signed Webhook Integrity
objects.summary: Verify exact raw request bytes before parsing provider webhooks and deduplicate at provider-event and domain-message layers.
boundaries: Do not copy Meta-specific headers or signature format into Stripe, WhatsApp, or another provider without checking that provider contract.

objects.title: Permission-Scoped Sensitive Exposure
objects.summary: Sensitive fields must be gated at query, search, evidence loading, and DTO serialization layers rather than only hidden in response formatting.
boundaries: Current Meta implementation has confirmed gaps; use as a warning and design target, not as proof the repo already satisfies the pattern everywhere.

objects.title: Idempotent Legacy Migration
objects.summary: Legacy migrations should support dry-run, repeat-safe execution, audit markers, and idempotency tests before old models are retired.
boundaries: The Meta repo still has compatibility debt; this is a candidate pattern, not proof the migration is complete.

objects.title: Score Semantic Separation
objects.summary: AI confidence, commercial opportunity strength, and operational urgency are different concepts and should not collapse into one score.
boundaries: Observed in one AI CRM reference project; validate independently before promoting as a universal product rule.

objects.title: External Send Succeeded, Local Persistence Failed
objects.summary: An external provider call can succeed before local persistence or audit fails; treating the whole operation as failed risks duplicate sends and false state.
objects.prevention: Model provider success and local persistence as separate durable facts, with uncertain reconciliation states.

objects.title: Provider-ID Search Oracle
objects.summary: A hidden provider identifier can still leak if search predicates match it for users who are not allowed to see provider IDs.
objects.prevention: Gate sensitive search predicates with the same permission that governs sensitive output exposure.

objects.title: Stale Recovery Dead Runtime Code
objects.summary: A stale-job recovery function is not a production protection if the worker loop never invokes it.
objects.prevention: Verify the actual process loop calls recovery on a schedule or startup path, and test stale-lock recovery against a disposable DB.

objects.title: Leads Evidence Bypasses Intelligence Permission
objects.summary: A route can enforce a broad leads permission while loading and serializing AI evidence that should require intelligence-specific permission.
objects.prevention: Test route-level permission boundaries, not only DTO helpers.

objects.title: Same-Person AI Snapshot Race
objects.summary: Concurrent AI jobs for the same entity can finish out of order and allow older analysis to overwrite newer durable memory.
objects.prevention: Serialize per entity or use version/updated-at guards inside the transaction.

objects.title: Test Expectation Drifts From Privacy Policy
objects.summary: Tests can encode stale expectations, such as expecting raw provider IDs while the privacy policy now defaults to masking.
objects.prevention: Keep tests tied to canonical privacy policy and update fixtures when masking defaults change.

objects.title: Temporary Adapter Production Drift
objects.summary: Temporary webhook/OAuth adapters can diverge from the intended owned-server production path and become false readiness evidence.
objects.prevention: Track adapter boundaries explicitly and require production-path evidence before readiness claims.

objects.title: Weak Commit Provenance
objects.summary: Repeated low-information commit messages erase intent and reduce future learning value even when code history exists.
objects.prevention: Use commit and run summaries that state intent, risk, and verification evidence.
